narratives.description: Systematic approach to market scanning and IPP assessment

narrativeContexts.context: Market opportunity identification scans customer demand patterns, competitive gaps, and technology evolution to identify white space where partner ecosystem expansion accelerates penetration or solution completeness.

Collaborate with product management and field sales teams to identify market segments and technology domains. Apply Ideal Partner Profile (IPP) assessment framework evaluating technical capabilities, market presence, financial viability, and cultural alignment. Develop business case models projecting partner-sourced ARR, market access value, and strategic alignment scores. Prioritize opportunities using multi-dimensional portfolio ranking balancing Total Opportunity Value, strategic fit, competitive urgency, and implementation complexity.

Avoid opportunistic partnerships without rigorous IPP validation. Ensure business case includes conservative scenario modeling. Do not underestimate resource requirements for partner onboarding and enablement.

narrativeContexts.context: Revenue model design shifts incentives from transaction-focused bookings to consumption-focused ARR recognition, aligning partner economics with customer success and recurring revenue.

Analyze partner business models (Reseller, CCSP, ISV, GSI) to understand revenue generation structures. Design partner-type-specific incentive models balancing partner profitability with vendor revenue retention. Emphasize consumption-based rebates, renewal incentives, and milestone-based payments tied to customer activation thresholds. Integrate CRM, usage data, and partner portal systems for automated deal registration, consumption tracking, and incentive calculation. Enable self-service earnings visibility and dispute resolution workflows.

Avoid transactional booking incentives that misalign with consumption economics. Do not overcomplicate incentive rules creating partner confusion. Ensure competitive parity with other vendor programs to maintain partner engagement.

narrativeContexts.context: Performance tracking infrastructure integrates CRM, partner portal, marketing automation, and billing systems creating unified partner performance views with real-time dashboards and structured Quarterly Business Reviews.

Configure data integration from CRM (deal registration, pipeline, win/loss), partner portal (training, certifications, marketing participation), and billing systems (consumption data). Build QBR scorecards comparing actuals against PSP commitments across financial, technical, marketing dimensions. Conduct gap analysis identifying underperforming areas requiring root cause investigation. Use cohort analysis comparing performance across partner segments. Develop predictive models forecasting partnership trajectory enabling proactive interventions. Trigger automated enablement campaigns or technical support based on performance pattern matching.

Avoid data silos preventing unified performance views. Do not rely on lagging indicators only, implement early warning systems. Ensure QBR preparation is data-driven, not anecdotal. Balance accountability with support, performance reviews should identify blockers, not just assign blame.

narratives.name: Co-Sell Technique
narratives.description: Co-sell orchestration approach

narrativeContexts.context: Co-sell orchestration coordinates matrixed partner and vendor sales teams through account mapping, deal registration workflows, and joint account planning ensuring pipeline transparency and conflict prevention.

Account mapping processes use CRM data synchronization with fuzzy name matching and relationship graph analysis identifying customer overlap, enabling warm introduction pathways through privacy-preserving protocols. Deal registration workflows protect partner-sourced opportunities through registration submission capturing opportunity details, approval workflows validating legitimacy, and protection period granting exclusive crediting window (90-180 days). Joint account planning templates structure coordinated multi-threading with role clarity matrix documenting relationship ownership, engagement strategy defining partner-led vs vendor-led coordination, and activity coordination calendar synchronizing meeting schedules avoiding customer confusion.

Avoid late deal registration creating crediting disputes; ensure transparent communication protocols preventing uncoordinated customer outreach; prevent territory overlap conflicts through clear geographic and vertical boundary definitions.
